body:
You are drafting DIALOGUE LINES for a video game. Reply in plain text only, in the exact format asked. No commentary.

## The game
"The Crooked Moon" is a single-player turn-based tactical party RPG (fully voiced, branching dialogue, skill checks, a storyteller Narrator). Folk-horror campaign set in Druskenvald, an afterlife realm of endless night under a gargantuan crescent moon with a leering crone's face. Drawn like a 1960s monster cartoon stuck in Halloween, but the story is real folk horror: stakes, doomed innocents, sacrifice. Humour is deadpan and sits inside the dread. Everything is our own invention in our own words.

## This chapter: Maidenmist Cemetery
South-east of the village of Wickermoor, an endless fogbound cemetery fenced with cold iron is really a prison built over a tear into the Shroud, the mist of death that rings the realm. Wrathful soul-stripped spirits called the shrouded would pour out of it. Its sexton is YORGRIM, the ghost of an orc seer of the Shadestone Clan, who was tricked by his chieftain into a ritual that annihilated his whole clan's souls; he drags a gravestone carved with their names chained to his back as penance. He is dour, stoic, few words, never cruel, tells what matters, and grows vaguer and more distracted as the chapter goes; deep slow orc bass, short flat sentences, long pauses. His spectral black hound ISOLDE (white eyes, a hooded lantern in her mouth) does not speak: only the Narrator describes her. He asked five friends to kindle balefire beacons from fragments of their souls: Sir Marius Renathyr (knight of a morning god, horse Dawn, King Viktor Denathria), Lethica Nightborne (priestess of the Nightmother, barn owl, loved Marius), Ol' Jericho Sticks (kindly scarecrow banjo man), Captain Briggsy Kratch (pirate with a heart of gold, lucky, a swordsman and schemer), Farryn of the Greenwood (satyr druid of the Green Queen, loved Gwenna). They fell to the Horned King's sin and the heroes (the player's party of four, level nine) killed them. The beacons went dark, the tear grew, the dead walked into Wickermoor. The heroes relight the beacons with Final Rites that honour who the Fallen were before they fell, then go below, where Yorgrim breaks and becomes the Chained Reaper; they destroy him and perform his own rites to seal the tear.
Wickermoor people: MORI SHADE, undertaker, grave, stately, white hair, all black, a fount of folklore, follows the Strangers' ways learned from Yorgrim; DORIS SQUIRE, constable, tall, stocky, says the fewest words possible, flat northern burr; TOBIAS DIBBS, Mori's apprentice, relentlessly cheerful and practical; HESTER BOLTON, annoyed her husband Gregor is now a ghast and still owes rent; ADELA DRUSKENVALD (transatlantic 1920s patter); WESTON MURDOCH (warm revival preacher); Theodora Mayville the postmaster is secretly a pigeon hag.

## The Narrator
The Narrator is the Vagrant, a frog-faced ferryman telling the tale afterwards: warm, folksy, wry, fond of the party; never gloats. Second person, present tense, only what a hero could perceive, concrete senses (smell, sound, texture), no game words (HP, roll, level, check, DC, save), no modern slang, never "suddenly". Never name a specific hero (the party is addressed as "you" or "the party").

## Format rules
- One line of plain text per key, written as `key: text`. No quotes around the text, no stage directions, no asterisks, no emoji, no em dashes (use commas, periods, colons), straight quotes only, no brackets.
- A spoken line is one to three short sentences, 12 to 38 words, never over 45. Narrator lines are one or two sentences, never over 45 words. People speak plainly in their own voice; they do not explain the plot to the audience.
- Obey each brief's sentence count and content. Every line must carry a concrete detail.
- Do not put speaker names at the start of the text. Do not repeat the brief.


## Lines to draft (key | speaker | mood | brief). Reply with one `key: text` line for each key and nothing else.

emerald_done | Narrator | - | The Emerald beacon roars up and the mist rolls back from Y8, the Burial Mounds; far off a sconce catches above the sepulcher doors. Two sentences.
emerald_thanks | yorgrim | smile | Yorgrim, quietly moved, honours Farryn of the Greenwood as who he was before he fell. Two short sentences.
emerald_all_lit | yorgrim | weary | All five are burning with his azure; Yorgrim says the sepulcher doors will open; it is time to go back. Two short sentences.
gate_arrive | Narrator | - | The party reaches the Maidenmist gate: the iron fence running into fog, the bent gate between two hooded reapers, the cold. Two sentences.
gate_rook | name:rook_coldwake | - | Rook Coldwake, clipped and deadpan with municipal vocabulary, remarks on the state of this fence as a piece of civic infrastructure. One line.
gate_chain | Narrator | - | A fifty-foot iron chain lies snapped in the mud by the gate; the links are bent outward. One or two sentences.
chain_clever | Narrator | - | The links were burst from inside; whatever broke the gate was already within. One or two sentences.
chain_plain | Narrator | - | The chain is old and cold and tells the party nothing more. One sentence.
chain_take | Narrator | - | The party coils fifty feet of cold iron over a shoulder; the chain is heavy and it feels right. One sentence.
mile1 | Narrator | - | In the first mile the fog leans on the party and every grave marker seems to look back; a wail sets in behind the eyes. Two sentences.
mile1_ok | Narrator | - | The party grits its teeth through the wail and comes through with only a headache. One sentence.
mile1_fail | Narrator | - | The wailing and the cold get through, and every hero staggers with it. One or two sentences.
mile3 | Narrator | - | The third mile is the coldest; breath hangs in the air and does not come back out. One or two sentences.
mile3_ok | Narrator | - | The party pushes through the freezing fog and reaches the hilltop with strength to spare. One sentence.
mile3_fail | Narrator | - | The cold settles into the bones and will not leave for a good while. One sentence.
kings_rest | Narrator | - | Before the rune-covered doors, wights and shrouded fight on in the fog without end, under a giant armoured king with his sword raised. One or two sentences.
kings_yorgrim | yorgrim | afraid | Yorgrim, flatly, warns them off; the doors kill; something sleeps inside that must not be woken. Two short sentences.
kings_doors | Narrator | - | The great doors do not budge; and the party is quite sure it would be a mistake if they did. One sentence.
arrive | Narrator | - | At the sepulcher's doors an orc ghost hunches under a chained gravestone, a black hound beside him, both holding lanterns to the seam. One or two sentences.
meet_hello | yorgrim | weary | Yorgrim, deep slow orc bass, short flat sentences, long pauses: he greets the strangers, says the dead have been restless, and asks who they are. Two short sentences.
q_who | yorgrim | neutral | Yorgrim says his name, that this is his cemetery, and that he serves the dead. Two short sentences.
q_place | yorgrim | neutral | Yorgrim says the hollow's dead have lain here for centuries, before him and after. Two short sentences.
q_dead | yorgrim | weary | Yorgrim says his life ended but his duty did not, and will not until he atones. Two short sentences.
q_dog | Narrator | - | The black hound with white eyes presses against Yorgrim's leg, a hooded lantern in her mouth with a spark in it. One sentence.
q_dog_line | yorgrim | smile | Yorgrim says she is Isolde, a grim, his only companion. One short sentence.
q_shroud | yorgrim | afraid | Yorgrim says the Shroud is death itself, an element that should not be here, not even in an afterlife. Two short sentences.
q_shrouded | yorgrim | angry | Yorgrim says shrouded are souls eaten and hollowed by the Shroud, abominations; do not let them touch you. Two short sentences.
q_friends | yorgrim | sad | Yorgrim says those the party killed were his friends, good hearts once, who fell to their burdens as anyone might. Two short sentences.
q_honour | yorgrim | neutral | Yorgrim says nobody will mourn the Crimson Abbot or the Grinning Sinner; he honours who those souls were while there was light in them, the only way. Two short sentences.
briefing_scene | Narrator | - | Yorgrim lifts his lantern; the fog backs off; the mist leaks from the seam in the doors and burns in the azure light. One sentence.
briefing_1 | yorgrim | weary | Yorgrim explains: the tear is growing; the beacons went out one by one; only his azure one still burns, tied to his soul. Three short sentences.
briefing_2 | yorgrim | neutral | Yorgrim explains: the rites of the Fallen can relight the other five; corrupted monsters guard the braziers; he will go with them and shield them with his light. Three short sentences.
briefing_3 | yorgrim | neutral | Yorgrim explains: Isolde stays at the door and can last only sixteen hours; when all six burn, the doors will open. Two short sentences.
accept_acolyte | yorgrim | smile | Yorgrim, gruffly pleased, says that will help. One short sentence.
result:
emerald_done: Green fire roars up from the brazier, driving the pale mist back from the turf of the burial mounds. Far off through the dark, a fifth sconce catches with emerald flame high above the sepulcher doors.
emerald_thanks: Farryn loved the green wood and his Gwenna more than his own breath. The moss and the roots remember his gentle hand now.
emerald_all_lit: Five flames burn beside my cold blue light once more. The heavy stone doors will yield to us now, so let us walk back.
gate_arrive: A spiked fence of black cold iron runs off into the clammy fog on either hand, bitter to the touch. Before you, the gate hangs twisted off its hinges between two stone pillars carved like hooded reapers.
gate_rook: From a strictly municipal standpoint, this perimeter fencing represents a catastrophic failure of township maintenance and boundary compliance.
gate_chain: Fifty feet of thick iron chain lies snapped in the black mud beside the gatepost. Its rusted links are wrenched open and bent outward toward the road.
chain_clever: Looking closer at the sheared iron, you see the heavy links were burst outward from the cemetery side. Whatever broke through this gate was already locked inside the fence.
chain_plain: The broken iron is old and freezing to the touch, and it tells you nothing more than that.
chain_take: You coil fifty feet of freezing, mud-slick iron over a shoulder, and the dead weight of it feels strangely reassuring.
mile1: In the first mile, the wet fog leans against your shoulders like sodden wool and every tilted headstone seems to turn its face toward you. A thin, reed-like wail sets in right behind your eyes.
mile1_ok: You grit your teeth against the ringing in your skulls and push through with nothing worse than a dull headache behind your brows.
mile1_fail: The keen of the dead bores through bone and ear alike, and the graveyard cold sinks into your chests until every one of you staggers in the mud.
mile3: The third mile is the coldest of all, smelling of wet slate and old pennies. Your breath hangs white in the dead air and feels as though it never quite comes back out.
mile3_ok: You keep your cloaks tight and march through the freezing mist, cresting the dark hilltop with breath and strength to spare.
mile3_fail: The cemetery frost settles deep into the marrow of your bones, leaving a leaden ache that will not leave you for a good long while.
kings_rest: Before a pair of rune-scarred stone doors, armored wights and hollow-eyed shrouded hack at one another in the mist without end. Above the fray stands the weathered statue of a giant king, his broadsword raised to the moon.
kings_yorgrim: Step away from those carved stones if you value your breath. The wards on that threshold kill, and what sleeps behind the iron must never wake.
kings_doors: The great rune-carved doors do not budge a hair under your hands, and a cold prickle in your palms tells you it would be a grave mistake if they did.
arrive: Before the great sepulcher doors, the pale ghost of an orc hunches beneath a gravestone chained across his back, a spectral black hound at his boot. Both hold hooded lanterns close to the stone seam.
meet_hello: Few living boots walk this wet gravel anymore, and the dead beneath the sod have grown restless. Tell me who you are, strangers, and why you come.
q_who: My name is Yorgrim, and I keep the iron keys to Maidenmist. I watch over the quiet dead who rest beneath this fog.
q_place: The dead of the hollow have lain under these mossy stones for centuries. They were buried here long before my time, and more will follow after.
q_dead: My breath ended long ago, but the chain on my back remains. My watch does not end until every name carved in this stone is answered for.
q_dog: The great black hound with milk-white eyes presses her shoulder against Yorgrim's spectral knee, holding a hooded iron lantern in her jaws where a tiny spark still glows.
q_dog_line: Her name is Isolde, a faithful churchyard grim, and the only soul who still walks beside me in the dark.
q_shroud: The Shroud is raw, unmaking death itself, creeping in like grey rot from the edge of the world. Such cold hunger does not belong here, not even in a realm of the dead.
q_shrouded: The shrouded are poor spirits chewed hollow by that grey mist until only spite remains in their husks. They are abominations now, so do not let their cold fingers touch your skin.
q_friends: Those five you cut down in the dark were my friends once, and they carried warm, honest hearts. Their burdens grew too heavy in the end, as any soul's burden might.
q_honour: No one in this valley will shed a tear for the Crimson Abbot or the Grinning Sinner. I remember the clear light they held before the rot took them, because there is no other way.
briefing_scene: Yorgrim raises his iron lantern high, forcing the grey fog back a pace as foul mist leaks from the seam of the sepulcher doors and hisses in his azure light.
briefing_1: The tear in the stone below us widens every hour. Five balefires went dark in the mist, one by one. Only my azure flame still burns above the door, bound to my own tattered soul.
briefing_2: The final rites of my fallen friends can wake the five cold braziers. Twisted beasts prowl around the stones to guard them. I will walk with you and hold the fog back with my light.
briefing_3: Isolde will stay by the threshold with her spark, though her strength will last only sixteen hours. When all six beacons burn against the sky, these stone doors will open.
accept_acolyte: An extra pair of steady hands with a lantern will serve us well in the deep fog.
